text:
Alex P.: heads up — I merged the new runtime metrics dashboard (https://grafana/redwood/d/runtime-infra) but we need to finalize alerting + pager routing before we flip it to prod. Can we align on thresholds and who owns what?

Maya R.: thanks. quick recap of what dashboard surfaces: p95/p99 latency, request queue length, KV cache hit ratio, per-model token throughput, and SLO burn rate panels. Also error rate broken down by error_type (oom, model-timeout, rpc).

Rana S.: for paging, my vote: infra-oncall (eng-runtime) for infra-level alerts (OOMs, node unreachable, massive queue growth). Platform-oncall for SLO burn alerts and dashboard regressions tied to config/rollouts.

Jess L.: +1 to separation. Can we avoid noisy per-model pages? We should group alerts by cluster or deployment tag, not by model_version. For tenants we might want per-customer routing but only for paid Dedicated accounts — otherwise it's noise.

Alex P.: agreed. Proposed concrete thresholds:
- error_rate (5m sum errors / sum requests) > 1% => P2 alert to platform-oncall
- p95 latency (5m window) > 400ms for > 5m => P3 but escalate if sustained 30m
- request_queue_length > 500 (cluster-wide) => P1 to eng-runtime
- KV cache hit ratio < 70% for 10m => P3 to platform (investigate rollout/quantization change)
- SLO burn rate: error_budget_burn_rate > 5x over 1h => P1 to platform with immediate incident template

Maya R.: can you drop PromQL examples so we can add to the alert rule files?

Rana S.: sure. rough drafts: 
- error_rate: sum(increase(runtime_errors_total[5m])) / sum(increase(runtime_requests_total[5m])) > 0.01
- p95 latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(runtime_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, cluster)) > 0.4
- queue: sum(runtime_request_queue_length) by (cluster) > 500
- kv hit: sum(runtime_kv_cache_hits) / sum(runtime_kv_cache_requests) < 0.7 over 10m
- burn: increase(error_budget_consumed[1h]) / increase(error_budget_total[1h]) > 5.0

Jess L.: burn formula looks aggressive but ok for P1. We need a runbook link for SLO-burn P1 that lists immediate steps (check recent rollouts, model variant fallback, increase capacity). I'll add a stub: https://wiki.redwood/slo-burn-runbook

Alex P.: good. On routing: we need PD mapping:
- P1 (SLO-burn, queue, OOM spike) -> eng-runtime escalation policy -> eng-sre primary, then eng-runtime, then eng-platform
- P2 (error rate surge) -> eng-platform primary -> eng-runtime secondary
- P3 (kv/cache, latency blips) -> platform triage rota only

Maya R.: small ask: include a label on alerts: 'impact_area' = {"runtime","platform","model-serving"} so dashboards/ops can filter. Also add 'deployment_id' and 'model_family' as grouping keys for debugging but not for routing.

Rana S.: agree. grouping: keep grouping_keys = [cluster, deployment_id] so we don't page on every model_version.

DevOps Bot: integrated: New dashboard "runtime-infra-metrics" created by alex-p; PR: #5423; alert rules pending review. :gear:

Jess L.: timeline: we want to flip on alerts and enable paging by EOD Wed. Can everyone review the alert rule PR? I will own the PR and update runbooks.

Alex P.: I'll open the PR for alert rules (prometheus/alerts/runtime.rules.yml) and add templates for PD escalation. Tentative PR link: https://git.redwood/runtime/pull/5580

Maya R.: one more thing — for canary rollouts we should have a special policy: if a rollout doubles p95 for canary group only (and not prod), alert to rollout-owner (product-play) and platform triage channel but do not page SRE immediately. Add a label rollout=canary and severity=low for those.

Rana S.: agreed. we'll add a condition to suppress paging if rollout=canary and affected_replicas < 5. Implemented via labels in the alert rule.

Alex P.: action items:
- Alex: open PR with rules + PD mappings + labels (today)
- Jess: populate runbook and incident template (today)
- Maya: review grouping keys and threshold math (tomorrow)
- Rana: add routing policies to PD escalation policy doc (tomorrow)

Jess L.: filing follow-up: I'll send a short note to eng-oncall about the expected changes to routing so oncall knows what hits to expect.

Maya R.: thanks everyone. one last ask: add a Grafana alert panel to the dashboard that shows current active pages (pd_current_incidents) so oncall can see noise level.

Alex P.: good idea — will add it to the dashboard panels. :thumbsup:

Rana S.: lgtm. tagging @eng-sre for visibility.

DevOps Bot: PR merged (runtime/alerts#5580) — 2 new alert groups added.

Alex P.: closing out — flipping alerting to prod in 30m after verifying no noisy fires in staging. If you see anything odd ping here or escalate to PD.

Jess L.: thanks — standby to cut the runbook link into the PD incident template. :white_check_mark:
